source.title: AP Psychology Prep Plus 2020–2021
source.integration: Additive layer; existing core notes and verified PYQ material are preserved.

microtopics.Metacognitive knowledge:
Kaplan frames metacognition as thinking about one's own cognitive processes. Focus on what you know about how you learn and which strategies fit the task.
Exam lens: distinguish knowledge about cognition from regulation/monitoring of cognition.
microtopics.Metacognitive regulation:
Kaplan separates metacognitive regulation from simply knowing about cognition. Regulation involves monitoring and adjusting the way you approach learning or problem solving.
Exam lens: checking understanding and changing strategy indicates regulation.
microtopics.Basic reinforcement variables:
Kaplan treats reinforcement as a core mechanism in operant learning: consequences can increase the likelihood that a behavior will occur again. Keep reinforcement separate from punishment, which is used to decrease behavior.
Exam lens: identify whether the consequence is intended to increase or decrease the target behavior.
microtopics.Reinforcement schedules:
Kaplan emphasizes ratio versus interval and fixed versus variable schedules. Fixed schedules are predictable; variable schedules change unpredictably.
Exam lens: first decide whether reinforcement depends on number of responses or passage of time, then whether the pattern is fixed or variable.
microtopics.James-Lange theory:
Kaplan presents James-Lange as a theory in which physiological arousal occurs before the experienced emotion.
Exam lens: physiological response → experienced emotion.
microtopics.Canon-Bard theory:
Kaplan contrasts Cannon-Bard with James-Lange in its treatment of emotion and physiological arousal.
Exam lens: simultaneous emotional experience and physiological response.
microtopics.Schachter and Singer theory:
Kaplan presents the two-factor approach as combining physiological arousal with cognitive interpretation or labeling of the situation.
Exam lens: arousal plus cognitive labeling, not arousal alone.
microtopics.Transactional Analysis:
Kaplan includes Transactional Analysis within psychotherapy. Keep it distinct from psychoanalysis, person-centered therapy and behavior therapy.
Exam lens: identify the approach from its characteristic terminology.
microtopics.Measures of central tendency:
Kaplan treats mean, median and mode as the main measures of central tendency. They describe the center of a distribution and are not interchangeable when data are skewed or contain outliers.
Exam lens: know what each statistic represents and how an outlier can affect the mean.
microtopics.Validity:
Kaplan distinguishes validity from reliability and lists content validity and criterion-related validity, including concurrent and predictive forms.
Exam lens: validity concerns whether an assessment measures what it is intended to measure.
microtopics.Semantic differential scale:
Kaplan includes the semantic differential scale among attitude measurement methods. It records evaluations along bipolar adjective dimensions.
Exam lens: recognize bipolar adjective formats and distinguish them from Likert agreement statements.
microtopics.Neuron structure:
Kaplan's biological review emphasizes basic neuron organization and the nervous system. Learn structural parts together with their functions rather than as isolated labels.
Exam lens: connect structure with information reception or transmission.
microtopics.Neuron functions:
Kaplan emphasizes neurons as part of systems that receive, process and transmit information.
Exam lens: distinguish the role of a neuron from the role of a neurotransmitter.
microtopics.Types of neurons:
Kaplan distinguishes major neuron types and relates them to information flow. Keep sensory/afferent, motor/efferent and interneuron roles distinct.
Exam lens: identify the direction of information flow first.
microtopics.Neural impulse:
Kaplan treats neural communication as an electrical process within the neuron followed by communication across the synapse.
Exam lens: distinguish the neural impulse within the neuron from chemical transmission between neurons.
microtopics.Synaptic transmission:
Kaplan emphasizes neurotransmitter activity in communication across the synapse and notes that drugs can influence neurotransmitters.
Exam lens: distinguish presynaptic release, synaptic transmission and postsynaptic effects.
microtopics.Neurotransmitters:
Kaplan treats neurotransmitters as chemical messengers in neural communication and links them to psychoactive-drug effects.
Exam lens: distinguish a neurotransmitter from a brain structure and from a hormone.
microtopics.Assumptions of signal detection theory:
Kaplan includes signal-detection theory in perception and emphasizes that detection depends on more than a fixed sensory threshold; sensitivity and decision processes matter.
Exam lens: separate perceptual sensitivity from response or decision tendencies.
microtopics.Applications of signal detection theory:
Kaplan uses signal-detection theory to explain decisions about whether a signal is present against background information.
Exam lens: identify the signal, background/noise and decision response.
microtopics.Observational learning:
Kaplan contrasts observational learning with classical and operant conditioning and uses Bandura's Bobo doll work as an example of learning through observing a model.
Exam lens: direct reinforcement of the learner is not required for observational learning to occur.
microtopics.Cognitive Dissonance:
Kaplan includes cognitive dissonance among major social-psychological processes. Focus on tension created by inconsistency among cognitions, attitudes or behavior and attempts to reduce that inconsistency.
Exam lens: identify the conflicting elements first.
microtopics.Social loafing:
Kaplan distinguishes social loafing from related group processes. It concerns reduced individual effort when people work collectively rather than being individually accountable.
Exam lens: look for reduced effort in a group task.
microtopics.Social Facilitation:
Kaplan contrasts social facilitation with social loafing. Social facilitation concerns how the presence of others can affect performance; social loafing concerns reduced effort in group work.
Exam lens: ask whether the question is about performance or effort contributed to a group.
microtopics.HIV/AIDS:
Kaplan places HIV/AIDS within health and health behaviour. Study it in the context of health-related behaviour and prevention as well as the disease label.
Exam lens: distinguish health behaviour/prevention concepts from the disease definition.
microtopics.Health-promoting behaviors:
Kaplan includes health-promoting behaviours as part of health and health behaviour.
Exam lens: classify a behaviour by whether it supports health and prevention.
microtopics.Poverty:
Kaplan discusses poverty within social and health-related contexts. Keep poverty as a social condition distinct from purely individual explanations.
Exam lens: do not reduce a structural/social condition to an individual characteristic.
microtopics.Perception of depth:
Kaplan identifies depth perception and binocular cues such as convergence and retinal disparity.
Exam lens: convergence and retinal disparity are binocular cues; distinguish them from monocular and motion cues.
microtopics.Perception of movement:
Kaplan describes stroboscopic motion as apparent movement produced by rapidly presented, slightly different static images.
Exam lens: stroboscopic motion is an example of apparent movement.
microtopics.Interference theory:
Kaplan lists proactive and retroactive interference under memory and forgetting.
Exam lens: proactive = earlier information interferes with newer learning; retroactive = newer information interferes with earlier information.
microtopics.Multiple regression:
Kaplan's statistics framework treats regression as a method for modeling relationships and making predictions; multiple regression uses more than one predictor.
Exam lens: distinguish prediction/association from experimental causation.
microtopics.Sampling:
Kaplan emphasizes the distinction between sampling and assignment. Sampling concerns selection from a population; random assignment concerns placement into experimental conditions.
Exam lens: sampling relates to generalization; random assignment relates to experimental group formation.
microtopics.Flow:
Kaplan includes flow within positive and applied psychology. Treat it as a distinctive state of highly engaged activity rather than a generic synonym for happiness.
Exam lens: identify the characteristic state described in the scenario.
microtopics.Leadership styles:
Kaplan places leadership styles within group dynamics and leadership. Study named styles and their characteristic behaviour without assuming one style is universally effective.
Exam lens: identify the leader's behaviour pattern first.
microtopics.Leadership effectiveness:
Kaplan treats leadership effectiveness as distinct from leadership style; effectiveness can depend on how leadership behaviour interacts with the group or situation.
Exam lens: do not equate a named style automatically with effectiveness.
microtopics.Item writing:
Kaplan's testing material treats item writing as part of test construction. The focus is constructing items that assess the intended distinction clearly.
Exam lens: distinguish writing an item from analyzing an administered item's performance.
microtopics.Item analysis:
Kaplan separates item analysis from item writing. Item analysis examines how individual test items function during test development.
Exam lens: questions about difficulty or discrimination of an existing item point to item analysis.
microtopics.Intelligence tests:
Kaplan lists IQ and the Wechsler scales, including WAIS and WISC, within intelligence testing.
Exam lens: WAIS is the adult scale; WISC is the child scale.
microtopics.Sleep:
Kaplan distinguishes NREM and REM sleep and includes related sleep phenomena and disorders.
Exam lens: identify the sleep feature described before selecting the stage or phenomenon.
microtopics.Long-term memory:
Kaplan distinguishes long-term memory from sensory and short-term/working memory and further divides long-term memory into forms such as declarative and procedural memory.
Exam lens: first identify the storage system, then the relevant long-term-memory subtype.
microtopics.Heuristics:
Kaplan contrasts heuristics with algorithms and insight as problem-solving approaches. Heuristics are useful mental shortcuts but can contribute to systematic judgment errors.
Exam lens: a shortcut rather than a guaranteed step-by-step procedure indicates a heuristic.
microtopics.Reflexes:
Kaplan lists reflexes within motor development and early development. A reflex is an automatic response rather than a deliberately learned action.
Exam lens: distinguish an inborn reflex from learned motor behaviour.
microtopics.Randomized Block Designs:
Kaplan's experimental-design framework includes randomized block designs. The design organizes participants into relevant blocks before randomization so variation associated with the blocking characteristic can be controlled.
Exam lens: distinguish randomized block designs from completely randomized and repeated-measures designs.
microtopics.Measures of dispersion:
Kaplan's statistics review places variance and standard deviation under measures of dispersion. They describe spread rather than the center of a distribution.
Exam lens: central tendency = center; dispersion = spread.
microtopics.Simple linear regression:
Kaplan's regression material treats regression as a method for modeling relationships and making predictions. Simple linear regression uses one predictor.
Exam lens: do not interpret a regression relationship as proof of causation.
microtopics.Repeated Measures Design:
Kaplan's experimental-design framework distinguishes repeated-measures designs from designs using different participants in each condition. The same participants contribute data across conditions.
Exam lens: look for repeated participation of the same individuals.
microtopics.Health-compromising behaviors:
Kaplan places health-compromising behaviours alongside health-promoting behaviours. The distinction is functional: one supports health, the other increases health risk.
Exam lens: classify by health consequence.
microtopics.Lindsley theory:
Kaplan lists Lindsley's theory among theories of emotion. Keep it distinct from James-Lange, Cannon-Bard and Schachter-Singer rather than collapsing the theories into one account.
Exam lens: identify the theory from the mechanism described.
